jobs.title: Investment Banking, Managing Director, Equity Capital Markets - Healthcare
jobs.description:
Job Purpose:

BTIG seeks a Managing Director to lead and grow the Healthcare Equity Capital Markets (“ECM”) franchise within the Investment Banking platform. This senior role is responsible for originating and executing equity financing transactions across the healthcare sector, delivering strategic capital markets advice to corporate clients, and deepening relationships with institutional investors. The ideal candidate is a proven revenue producer with strong market judgment, executive-level presence, and the ability to lead teams in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment.
Duties & Responsibilities:

Source, develop, and maintain senior-level relationships with healthcare corporates, sponsors, and key ecosystem participants to drive new business.
Serve as a trusted advisor to C-suite executives and boards on equity financing strategy, market windows, investor positioning, and transaction structures.
Partner with sector and product leadership to build and execute annual business plans, revenue targets, and client coverage priorities.
Lead end-to-end execution of equity and equity-linked transactions including IPOs, follow-ons, confidentially marketed offerings, registered directs, PIPEs/private placements, at-the-market programs, and block trades (as applicable).
Oversee deal strategy, syndicate coordination, investor targeting, marketing approach, and pricing recommendations in partnership with Sales/Trading and Syndicate.
Ensure high-quality, accurate, and timely delivery of marketing and transaction materials (e.g., pitch decks, CIMs, investor presentations, management scripts).
Direct the development of sector and market content for corporate and institutional clients (market updates, relative value views, issuance trends, and positioning insights).
Use data-driven analytics to inform origination opportunities, client advice, and post-transaction follow-up.
Collaborate with Healthcare Investment Banking, Research, Sales & Trading, Corporate Access, and other product teams to maximize franchise impact and deliver a coordinated client experience.
Represent BTIG externally at conferences and industry events to strengthen brand visibility and client connectivity.
Lead, mentor, and develop junior bankers; set execution standards across modeling, materials, diligence support, and client communications.
Manage multiple live processes simultaneously while maintaining strong risk controls, compliance discipline, and attention to detail.

Requirements & Qualifications:

Must be based in (or willing to relocate to) the New York City area.
12+ years of relevant investment banking / ECM experience with significant healthcare transaction exposure; prior experience operating at senior coverage or ECM leadership level strongly preferred.
Demonstrated track record of origination and execution across healthcare equity financings (IPO and follow-on experience required; private placements preferred).
Strong client management skills with the ability to advise and influence senior executives.
Deep understanding of equity capital markets dynamics, investor behavior, and issuance processes.
Excellent analytical capabilities and strong command of financial statements/valuation; ability to guide (not necessarily produce) detailed modeling and analysis.
Outstanding written and verbal communication skills; strong presentation and storytelling ability.
Proven ability to lead teams, prioritize under pressure, and manage multiple concurrent transactions with precision.
High integrity and commitment to the highest ethical and compliance standards.
FINRA licenses

Important Notes:

Must be authorized to work full time in the U.S., BTIG does not offer sponsorship for work visas of any type
No phone calls please, the applicant will be contacted within two weeks if successful

About BTIG:

BTIG is a global financial services firm specializing in institutional trading, investment banking, research and related brokerage services. With an extensive global footprint and more than 700 employees, BTIG, LLC and its affiliates operate out of 20 cities throughout the U.S., and in Europe, Asia and Australia. BTIG offers execution, expertise and insights for equities, equity derivatives, ETFs and fixed income, currency and commodities. The firm’s core capabilities include global execution, portfolio, electronic and outsource trading, investment banking, prime brokerage, capital introduction, corporate access, research and strategy, commission management and more.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or disability status. BTIG is an equal opportunity employer Minorities/Females/People with Disabilities/Protected Veterans/Sexual Orientation/Gender Identity.
Compensation: 

BTIG offers a competitive compensation and benefits package. Salary range is based on a variety of factors including, but not limited to, location, years of applicable experience, skills, qualifications, licensure and certifications, and other business and organization needs.
The current estimated base salary range for this role is $300,000.00 - $400,000.00 per year. Please note that certain positions are eligible for additional forms of compensation such as discretionary bonus or overtime. 

Disclaimer: https://www.btig.com/disclaimer.aspx.

jobs.title: Director of Operations
jobs.description:
About The Run Rx

The Run Rx is a physical therapy and performance studio helping runners and active individuals recover from injury, build strength, and perform at a higher level.

We are known for exceptional care, meaningful client relationships, and a human-centered approach that blends healthcare, fitness, performance, and hospitality to redefine the healthcare experience. 

The Role

We’re looking for a Director of Operations to own the systems, people, and day-to-day execution that keep The Run Rx running at a high level.
This person will be the Owner’s primary operational partner—turning ideas into action, improving systems, supporting team performance, solving problems before they become bigger problems, and helping the business grow without sacrificing the quality or personal experience our staff and clients expect. We’re looking for someone who can independently think, decide, implement, and lead.

This will be a hybrid role combining in-person and remote work
. We expect more in-person involvement initially while learning the business, team, and systems, with the role likely becoming primarily remote over time
while maintaining regular clinic presence as needed.

Our ideal structure is approximately 25–30 hours per week
, but we are open to a full-time position for the right person and fit
.

What You’ll Own

Business systems, SOPs, workflows and operational improvements
HubSpot/CRM management, automations, reporting and technology implementation
Staffing capacity, schedules, hiring and onboarding assist
Performance management and team accountability alongside clinical leadership
Payroll, bill pay and operational oversight
High-level customer service and client communication
Inquiry follow-up, onboarding and client retention systems
Referral partnerships, community outreach and events
Clinic KPIs, performance trends and implementation of improvements
Day-to-day operational decisions that allow the Owner to stay focused on higher-level strategy

The Ideal Candidate

You may be a great fit if you:
Take initiative naturally and rarely need to be told what to do next
Problem-solve before escalating and bring solutions, not just questions
Are highly organized, dependable and accountable to results
Are deeply likable, emotionally intelligent and exceptionally customer-service oriented
Believe great service should feel radically human, hospitable and clear
Can make business decisions and translate them into systems and behaviors that support growth, client experience and clinical excellence
Are comfortable holding people accountable and having direct, respectful conversations
Understand how staffing, utilization, customer experience and financial performance connect
Are highly tech-savvy and comfortable learning and improving systems
Are comfortable with tools such as scheduling platforms, EMRs, Zapier, Google Workspace, payment systems and website platforms
Can move between strategic thinking and hands-on execution without getting stuck in either

Ideal experience

3-4+ years in an operations, business management or general manager role, including at least 1+ years directly managing people — not just coordinating a team or leading projects.
Have meaningful experience with HubSpot or another robust CRM
Has personally handled a disciplinary conversation, performance improvement plan, or termination.
Has owned or had visibility into a P&L or operating budget
Has implemented or overhauled a system or process end-to-end — not just used one someone else built. 
Experience in a small or single-location high touch business, ideally service-based (healthcare, fitness, hospitality, salon, boutique retail)

Compensation + Benefits

Competitive compensation based on experience, scope and weekly hours
Performance-based bonus opportunity tied to business growth and operational performance
401(k) with up to 3% employer match
Paid time off for eligible employees
Flexible hybrid work structure, with the role expected to become increasingly remote over time
Professional development and growth opportunities
Opportunity to take on increasing ownership and responsibility as the business grows

How to Apply

Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter answering:
Why do you think you’d be a great fit for The Run Rx and this role?
What are your top three strengths as an operator and leader?
Tell us about a time you identified a problem, built a solution, and improved performance or efficiency.
What experience do you have with HubSpot or other CRM/automation platforms?

Overview

At KeHE, we’re obsessed with creating solutions, unboxing potential, and serving others - and it all starts with you. As an employee-owned distributor of natural and organic, specialty, and fresh products, we’re committed to making a positive impact and scaling our success together. With a culture that fosters development and opportunity, you’ll be embarking on a career that’s moving forward. When you join KeHE, you’re becoming part of a team that is a force for good.

Primary Responsibilities

The Executive Director of Sales is a key leadership role and responsibility for planning, directing, and coordinating the development and execution of sales, marketing, and merchandising programs to retail stores and other retailers that meet regional and company financial goals. This position will also develop and solidify relationships with customers, vendors, and broker partners. As with all positions at KeHE we expect that all actions will be consistent with KeHE’s Mission, Vision, and Values.

Essential Functions

DUTIES, TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Develops and executes plans and programs to ensure sales and profit growth maximize at the account level through analytical and fact-based selling.

Ongoing sales plan development, assessment, analysis, and execution specific to the accounts of responsibility.
Increases sales by finding new business opportunities and through consistent follow up.
Responsible for the analysis and distribution of category management information and initiatives.
Participates in regional and national trade events and represents the company through public speaking and participation in industry associations.
Manages budgets for the assigned customers.
Monitors competitor activities and recommends paths forward to address these activities.
Works with a sense of urgency towards projects, requests, and deadlines.
Communicates and collaborates with other KeHE functional areas to meet all company objectives.
Assures that established company policies and procedures are followed in the assigned sales area.
Other duties and projects as assigned.

SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE AND ABILITIES:

Excellent communication skills including verbal, written and presentation with the ability to convey a clear understanding of unique needs of audiences.
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate effectively with cross functional teams to meet objectives.
Strong ability to lead teams and provide guidance and leadership.
Ability to focus on highest priorities and set aside less critical tasks.
Ability to plan and lay out a thorough schedule and steps for achieving objectives.
Ability to tackle obstacles and develop excellent contingency plans.
Quickly and decisively acts in fast-changing, unpredictable situations.
Exceptional at spotting or seizing opportunities.
Exhibits tremendous amount of initiative in tough situations.
Able to gain the confidence and trust of others through honesty, integrity, and authenticity.
Expresses self in credible and transparent manner, and models high standards of honesty and integrity with self, co-workers, and direct reports.
Ability to know the most effective and efficient processes to get things done with a focus on continuous improvement.
Holds self and others accountable to meet commitments.
Creates a climate where people are motivated to do their best and help the organization achieve its objectives and consistently achieve results, even under tough circumstances.
Build strong-identity teams that apply their diverse skills and perspectives to achieve common goals.
Ability to be courageous and address difficult issues and be willing to say what needs to be said and done.
Strong knowledge of sales and financial reports and understanding and interpreting of key financial indicators to make better business decisions.
Ability to understand complex, high quantity and at times contradictory information to effectively solve problems.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Excel, Access, Power BI).
Willingness to travel to various business locations up to 75% of time.
Ability and willingness to work flexible hours as needed, including some weekends.

Minimum Requirements, Qualifications, Additional Skills, Aptitude

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

Bachelor’s degree in Sales, Business, or a related field is required.
Minimum 12+ years of experience in the grocery retail channel with 8+ years of management experience.

jobs.title: Program Director
jobs.description:
The Program Director leads a team of Retail Program Managers responsible for delivering complex, multi-site retail implementation and transformation programs. Programs vary in scope, scale, complexity, and execution and require extensive cross-functional coordination across Adrenaline's broad portfolio of products and services.

This role provides strategic leadership and oversight across multiple enterprise-level implementation programs, driving program governance, operational excellence, standardized delivery practices, financial performance, and successful client outcomes. The Program Director is accountable for ensuring programs are delivered on time, within budget, to established quality standards, and in a manner that provides a best-in-class client experience. A strong understanding of Adrenaline's products, services, implementation methodologies, operational processes, and client engagement model is essential for success in this role.

Accountabilities

Lead, develop and collaborate with a high-performing team of Retail Program Managers, driving accountability, collaboration, and operational excellence.
Provide strategic oversight for multiple complex enterprise-level implementation programs, ensuring successful delivery of scope, schedule, budget, quality, and financial objectives.
Build and maintain executive-level client relationships, serving as a trusted advisor and sponsor to achieve successful business outcomes and long-term partnerships.
Establish governance, standards, and performance metrics that promote consistency, transparency, scalability, and continuous improvement.

Responsibilities

Manage the full program lifecycle, including planning, execution, resource management, budgeting, risk mitigation, issue resolution, and client acceptance.
Lead cross-functional collaboration among internal teams, clients, vendors, and stakeholders to drive alignment, decision-making, and successful program outcomes.
Monitor program performance through KPIs, reporting, dashboards, and executive communications, ensuring informed decision-making and delivery excellence.
Oversee scope, change, and financial management practices while balancing client objectives, operational feasibility, quality, and profitability.
Champion process improvements, standardized methodologies, AI-enabled productivity tools, and lessons learned to enhance delivery capabilities and organizational effectiveness.
Support business growth by strengthening client relationships and identifying opportunities to expand services.
Travel as required to support program and client needs.

Qualifications

10+ years of progressively responsible project and program management experience, including experience leading program management teams in complex client-facing environments.
Extensive experience leading large-scale, enterprise-level programs with responsibility for delivery, financial performance, risk management, and stakeholder engagement..
Experience working with financial institutions, including banks and credit unions, is strongly preferred.
Experience leveraging AI-powered productivity tools to enhance reporting, documentation, analysis, and workflow efficiency.
Expertise and advanced skills in program governance, reporting, operational excellence, process improvement, and data-driven decision-making.
Strong executive communication, client relationship management, and influencing skills across cross-functional organizations
Ability to manage multiple priorities, drive strategic initiatives, and deliver results in a fast-paced environment.

Adrenaline is an Equal Opportunity Employer and Prohibits Discrimination and Harassment of Any Kind. All employment decisions at Adrenaline are based on business needs, job requirements and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion or belief, national, social or ethnic origin, sex (including pregnancy), age, physical, mental or sensory disability, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, marital, civil union or domestic partnership status, past or present military service, family medical history or genetic information, family or parental status, or any other status protected by the laws or regulations in the locations where we operate. Adrenaline will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics.
